title: While using MWB, UAC popup on Win 10 "client" system causes various problems

judgment.rationale: The thread includes a service-mode workaround and a later contrary observation; they must be tested separately rather than marking the original problem resolved.
evidence: On 0.70 a Windows 10 client could not interact with UAC from the controlling Windows 11 machine.
A maintainer recommended service mode; the original reporter said another issue prevented it, while a later user reports service-mode UAC reconnects and returns the pointer.

Mouse Without Borders checks desktop switch events in https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/237dc893c8c76b1bfa65994afda41ea7315a914c/src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Core/WinAPI.cs, while service mode has a distinct lifecycle.

proposed_fixes.title: Investigate service-mode UAC reconnects
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The later service-mode reconnect may be a desktop-switch transition problem, distinct from the original inability to use service mode.
plan: Reproduce UAC on the controlled machine with service mode enabled and disabled using two test machines.
Observe desktop-switch and connection events without weakening UAC or altering secure-desktop security guarantees.
Fix any confirmed unintended reconnect or pointer restoration behavior, preserving the required privilege boundary.
verification: With supported service mode, a UAC transition does not unnecessarily strand the pointer or require a manual reconnect; non-service security restrictions remain intact.

An account able to approve a UAC prompt
setup: Configure the controlled client with service mode on, then repeat with it off.
steps: Trigger a normal UAC prompt and observe pointer and connection state.
